name: Brute Force
description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to attempt credential access by systematically guessing passwords, passphrases, or encryption keys. Variations include password guessing, password spraying, and credential stuffing.
detection: Monitor for numerous failed authentication attempts followed by a success from the same source IP or targeting multiple accounts within a short window (e.g., Windows Event ID 4625 followed by 4624, or repeated sshd Failed password).
mitigations: M1036: Account lockout policies after a threshold of failed attempts.
M1032: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) on all external facing portals.
M1027: Rate limiting and IP-based automated blocking using fail2ban or WAF.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Adversaries may attempt to exploit a weakness in an Internet-facing computer or program using software, firmware, or virtual machine flaws to gain access or execute arbitrary commands. Includes SQL Injection, Remote Code Execution (RCE), and Path Traversal.
detection: Analyze web server access logs for anomalous request payloads containing SQL keywords (UNION SELECT, OR 1=1), directory traversal patterns (../..), or non-standard user agents (sqlmap, Nikto).
mitigations: M1050: Exploit Protection and Web Application Firewall (WAF) rule sets.
M1016: Strict input validation and parameterized queries (prepared statements).
M1051: Timely security patch management for web servers and runtime dependencies.

name: Valid Accounts
tactic: Defense Evasion, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, Initial Access
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion. Compromised credentials can be default, local, or domain accounts.
detection: Correlate logins at abnormal hours or from unusual geographic IP addresses. Monitor Windows Event ID 4624 with unusual LogonType (e.g. Type 3 network logon to domain controllers from non-admin workstations) and Event ID 4672 (Special privileges assigned).
mitigations: M1026: Privileged Account Management and Just-In-Time (JIT) access.
M1030: Network segmentation restricting workstation-to-workstation access.
M1018: User account management and continuous credential auditing.

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts, including port scans (TCP SYN scans) or banner grabs, to identify vulnerable software versions.
detection: Detect high volume of connection attempts to sequential or distinct closed/filtered ports from a single IP address within firewall and IDS/IPS logs over a brief duration.
mitigations: M1030: Network segmentation and perimeter firewall egress/ingress filtering.
M1031: Network intrusion detection and automated dynamic blacklisting.

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
description: Adversaries may circumvent mechanisms designed to control elevate privileges to gain higher-level permissions (e.g. abusing sudo misconfigurations, setuid binaries, or Windows UAC bypass).
detection: Monitor audit logs for unexpected invocations of sudo, especially attempts to read sensitive files like /etc/shadow or /etc/sudoers (e.g., Linux pam_unix sudo auth failure followed by repeated attempts).
mitigations: M1026: Restrict sudoers permissions to specific necessary binaries with NOEXEC.
M1038: Execution prevention and SELinux / AppArmor mandatory access controls.
